title: Recursive sequences using only addition and subtraction can be complex

fields.label: Label
fields.value: Recursive sequences using only addition and subtraction can be complex

fields.label: Statement
fields.value: Recursive integer sequences whose rule refers back a variable distance (e.g. f[n - f[n - 1]]) and uses only addition and subtraction can produce fluctuations that are complex and in many respects random.

fields.label: Quotation
fields.value: even though the rules ultimately involve only addition and subtraction, they nevertheless correspond to programs that are capable of producing behavior of great complexity.

fields.label: Agent
fields.value: delphisci A New Kind of Science claim extractor

fields.label: Assumptions
fields.value: Stephen Wolfram, A New Kind of Science (Champaign, IL: Wolfram Media, 2002), Chapter 4, “Systems Based on Numbers”; section “Recursive Sequences” (from p. 128), p. 131. Scope: nested recursive integer sequences (Hofstadter-like sequences)

fields.label: Assessment
fields.value: GPT-5.6 Sol on wolfram2002-ch04-08: resolvable-now, resolvability 0.79

fields.label: Finding
fields.value: Public sequence records and direct computation provide the needed terms, and the claim's core is existential rather than universal. Standard analyses can show substantial finite complexity, though stronger stochastic interpretations remain test-relative.

fields.label: Proposed test in the assessment
fields.value: Proposed test with existing data: Compute named Hofstadter-like recurrences for long ranges and measure fluctuation spectra, predictability, compression, and departure from simple periodic or nested baselines. Robust examples using only addition and subtraction establish the existential capability claim.

fields.label: Evidence against
fields.value:
Random in many respects depends on selected statistics.

Some recurrences may become undefined or be difficult to extend.

fields.label: Dimension scores
fields.value:
data adequacy: 0.68
analysis feasibility: 0.9
discriminating power: 0.75
data existence: 0.9
operationalizability: 0.72

fields.label: Finding
fields.value: The sequences are integer recurrences with published terms and trivial recomputation, and Wolfram's own examples already separate nested cases from irregular ones. Showing that at least some addition-subtraction recurrences of this kind have fluctuations that fail periodicity and nesting tests settles the existence claim. Calling those fluctuations random 'in many respects' is a weaker, test-dependent gloss on that same computation.

fields.label: Proposed test in the assessment
fields.value: Proposed test with existing data: Evaluate nested recurrences that use only addition and subtraction, such as rules depending on f[n - f[n-1]], and test the fluctuations of f[n] for nesting versus statistical irregularity. An irregular fluctuation series confirms that such rules can be complex; every well-defined rule in the class reducing to a regular nested or periodic fluctuation would refute the 'can.'

fields.label: Evidence against
fields.value:
Some of these recurrences are known to be nested and are related to binary digits, so the randomness claim has to be restricted to the irregular cases.

Statistical irregularity of fluctuations does not identify the mechanism that produces them.

fields.label: Dimension scores
fields.value:
discriminating power: 0.6
analysis feasibility: 0.9
data adequacy: 0.75
data existence: 0.9
operationalizability: 0.7

fields.label: Hypothesis
fields.value: At least one of Wolfram's nested recurrences using only addition and subtraction, f[n] = f[p[n]] + f[q[n]] with variable look-back such as n - f[n-1], produces fluctuations about its trend that are incompressible (not periodic or nested) and sign-balanced, while his nested examples (c) and (d) are detected as highly compressible.

fields.label: Method
fields.value: analysis.py computes each of the six recurrences for n <= 2^20 with memoised integer arithmetic, verifies rules (e) and (c) term-by-term against the 10,000-term OEIS b-files of A005185 and A004001 (all terms match), detrends by n/2 (rules c-g) or by a log-log power-law fit for n >= 16 (rule h), lzma-compresses the increment-sign sequence of the residual, and measures sign balance and the dyadic correlation corr(r[n], r[2n]).

fields.label: Pass criterion
fields.value: Pre-registered. Rules (all with f[1]=f[2]=1, from NKS pp. 129-130): (c) f[n]=f[f[n-1]]+f[n-f[n-1]] (OEIS A004001); (d) f[n]=f[n-f[n-1]]+f[n-f[n-2]-1]; (e) f[n]=f[n-f[n-1]]+f[n-f[n-2]] (OEIS A005185); (f) f[n]=f[n-f[n-1]-1]+f[n-f[n-2]-1]; (g) f[n]=f[f[n-1]]+f[n-f[n-2]-1]; (h) f[n]=f[f[n-1]]+f[n-2f[n-1]+1]. Compute f[n] for n <= N = 2^20 (stop a rule if an index < 1 occurs). Residual r[n] = f[n] - n/2 for (c)-(g); for (h) r[n] = f[n] - a n^b with (a,b) a least-squares power-law fit in log-log. Statistics: (i) bits per symbol = 8 * lzma(preset 9|EXTREME) compressed size of the increment-sign sequence sign(r[n]-r[n-1]) in {-1,0,1} stored as one byte each, divided by N-1; (ii) sign balance |P(increment>0) - P(increment<0)|; (iii) dyadic self-similarity corr(r[n], r[2n]) for n in [N/4, N/2) (reported). A rule is 'complex/random-like' if it is well defined up to N, (i) >= 0.5 bits/symbol and (ii) <= 0.05. The claim PASSES if at least one of rules (e)-(h) is complex/random-like AND the nested controls (c) and (d) both have (i) < 0.15 bits/symbol (validity of the measure). Calibration from controls outside the family: binary digit sum s2(n) gives 0.002 bits/symbol, its partial sums 0.005, a symmetric random walk 1.10.

fields.label: Fail criterion
fields.value: Pre-registered. The claim FAILS if none of rules (e)-(h) is complex/random-like (every one is undefined before N, or compresses below 0.5 bits/symbol, or is sign-unbalanced by more than 0.05). If the nested controls (c) or (d) do not compress below 0.15 bits/symbol the measure lacks discriminating power and the verdict is inconclusive (not-operationalizable). If computed terms disagree with the OEIS b-files for A005185 or A004001, the verdict is inconclusive (other) until the implementation is fixed.

fields.label: Unit
fields.value: rules among (e)-(h) that are complex/random-like by the pre-registered criteria

fields.label: Interpretation
fields.value: 'Fluctuations ... complex and in many respects random' (p. 130-131) is read as: the increment-sign sequence of the detrended fluctuations is not compressible to a small fraction of its entropy bound by a general-purpose compressor (nested/digit-based fluctuations compress to < 0.01 bits/symbol), and positive and negative fluctuations are balanced (Wolfram's own stated 'respect' for case (f)). The claim is existential ('can produce'), so one qualifying rule suffices; the book's nested rules (c) and (d) serve as internal controls that must be detected as regular. The OEIS b-files provide independent public values of two of the sequences to verify the implementation. Trend n/2 for (c)-(g) follows the book's plots; the power-law trend for (h) follows the book's caption (0.42 n^0.916).

fields.label: Datasets
fields.value:
OEIS A005185 (Hofstadter Q-sequence) b-file

OEIS A004001 (Hofstadter-Conway $10000 sequence) b-file

Six nested recurrences from NKS pp. 129-130 (generated by analysis.py)

fields.label: Caveats
fields.value:
Statistical incompressibility over 2^20 terms is evidence of complexity, not proof that no closed form exists; the test shows the fluctuations are not periodic or nested at the scales examined.

Rules (g) and (h) have dyadic correlation corr(r[n], r[2n]) of 0.44 and 0.41 (vs 1.00 for nested rule c and ~0 for e, f), so part of their fluctuation is self-similar at scale 2; they still compress at > 0.97 bits/symbol, so the sign sequence itself carries no detectable regularity.

For rule (h) the power-law trend fitted over n in [16, 2^20] is 0.338 n^0.837, not the book's 0.42 n^0.916 fitted over n <= 2048; residual statistics for (h) depend mildly on the trend choice.

The sign-balance 'respect' is Wolfram's own stated one for case (f); other respects of randomness (e.g. spectral flatness, distribution of increments) were not pre-registered and not tested.

The downloaded b-files (about 97 KB each) are not committed; analysis.py re-fetches them and the SHA-256 values above pin what was used.
